title: Provide ID, sex and age of patient who has blood glucose (GLU) not within n
question: Provide ID, sex and age of patient who has blood glucose (GLU) not within normal range but with total cholesterol(T-CHO) within normal range.

auxiliary_raw_evidence_draft.base_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', p.Birthday) AS age
FROM PatientInfo AS p
JOIN Laboratory AS l
    ON p.ID = l.ID
WHERE (l.GLU < 70 OR l.GLU > 180)
  AND l.`T-CHO` < 250

scope_obligations: Eligibility rows: Laboratory observations for that patient with GLU outside normal range and T-CHO within normal range.
Returned fields: patient ID, sex, age.

checks: Eligible entity is patient (PatientInfo.ID), correctly joined to Laboratory via the certified FK Laboratory.ID = PatientInfo.ID.

Eligibility condition requires a single Laboratory row where GLU is outside normal range AND T-CHO is within normal range; this is the correct interpretation of 'has blood glucose not within normal range but with total cholesterol within normal range' as a co-occurring observation.
T-CHO < 250 is supported by historical SQL (1298: 'total cholesterol is within the normal range' → T-CHO < 250) and is consistent with observed T-CHO values (min 37, max 568).

GLU < 70 OR GLU > 180 is the only concrete normal-range hypothesis; observed GLU values span 62–499, making these bounds plausible. No historical SQL provides an explicit GLU normal-range threshold, so this remains an uncertainty.
DISTINCT is appropriate because a patient may have multiple qualifying Laboratory rows; the question asks for the patient, not the observation.

Age is derived from Birthday using year subtraction, which is the standard approach when no stored age column exists. This is a simplification (ignores month/day) but is the only available method given the schema.
scope_review.reason: No semantic correction is required: the submitted query correctly identifies patients with at least one laboratory observation where GLU is outside the 70–180 normal range and T-CHO is below the 250 normal-range threshold, and projects the requested ID, sex, and derived age. The T-CHO < 250 threshold is directly supported by historical SQL (question 1298) and the observed T-CHO value range (37–568). The GLU 70/180 bounds are the only concrete hypothesis available (observed GLU range 62–499), and no alternative thresholds are evidenced in the ontology. The query executes successfully and returns the expected columns.

    p.ID,

    CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER) - CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM PatientInfo AS p

WHERE (l.GLU < 70 OR l.GLU > 180)
